citations.review_text: "Ehhhh" is how I describe it. The art style, visuals, and memes are fun to look at but this game is just not exactly what I expected. I wish I could aim my main attack and actually do something with it. I can't quite explain it but it feels like its lacking just a tinge more input from me. Other "bullet heaven" type games feel better to play in my opinion.

I don't like this game, it feels like a slot machine with a single button, it just plays itself and your actions affect nothing. You can literally stand in one place and wait until it progresses all by itself up to the moment when you're supposed to end the run. The only thing that is needed from you is to occasionally click "Open" to open the lootbox. Don't recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running smoothly and performing well on laptops, low-spec hardware, and the Steam Deck.

citations.review_text: If you like Brotato, you`ll love this! Fast, chaotic and silly in the best way. It's a 3D survivors-style game where you run, jump and slide around while your weapons fire automatically, and you level up to pick new upgrades. Runs build up until the screen is full of effects and enemies melting away, which is so satisfying. There are plenty of characters and unlocks to chase. Ran smoothly on my laptop and steam deck even when things got crazy. Massive fun from a simple idea.

A nice survivors-like which has just enough depth to keep you coming back (not too much depth that you'd be stuck learning it), plus it runs perfectly on Deck. If I had any complaints it'd be that some characters feel over-tuned or under-tuned, balance is not consistent at all (but if you get lucky, you can still steamroll most everything), though I don't consider that a bad thing necessarily seeing what this game goes for
love it no notes will run on a potato

This game weirdly feels like something that should only be play on Steam Deck. Very satisfying and fast paced gameplay. Quick and easy to understand, and it runs flawlessly. I just love the feeling of playing it on Steam Deck though. Consider picking this game up.

Had a decent bit of fun with this. It definitely does more than just being Vampire Survivors in 3D (though it's that too). It focuses more on smaller areas and exploration which works well with the 3D physics and platforming. Can be funny to see tons of enemies literally piling on top of each other to get to you. It's all very silly and worth the price.

Unfortunately I hit a wall with progression and really couldn't figure out scaling my power enough to progress into the harder levels. In Vampire Survivors there was always more to see, discover and unlock - and it felt like most weapons could become absurdly powerful in almost any combination. In Megabonk though it felt like sometimes leveling up barely made a difference compared to the enemy power level. 

Still would be happy to come back to this for some more good times and will keep an eye on if there's any DLC

Megabonk is an addictively chaotic 3D roguelike survival game that successfully brings the frantic "bullet heaven" formula into a low-poly third dimension. Developed and published by vedinad, it drops players into procedurally generated maps where automatic weapon firing, chaotic hordes of enemies, and explosive meta-progression combine to create an experience that is impossible to put down.  

​The world design leans heavily into its charmingly lo-fi, meme-infused internet aesthetic. Environments are filled with verticality, slopes to slide down for momentum, hidden secrets, shrines, and dodgy merchants, making every run feel dense despite a relatively compact map count. Exploring the terrain and finding optimal positioning is just as vital as managing your gear.  

​Traversal and movement form the heartbeat of the gameplay loop. Because your arsenal attacks automatically, your primary focus is dodging, jumping, managing cooldowns, and staying airborne to trigger specific damage multipliers. Whether you are playing as a banana-tossing ninja monkey who can scale walls or a skateboarding skeleton, moving through the chaos feels snappy and responsive.
  
​Combat scaling is where Megabonk truly shines. As you defeat enemies and collect XP, you choose from randomized upgrade pools—combining character passives, weapons, mystical Tomes, and synergistic items. A successful run transforms your character from a fragile survivor into an absolute engine of destruction, filling the screen with particle effects, bouncing projectiles, and physics-defying chaos.  

​Enemy variety and boss encounters keep the pressure high. Hordes pile on top of each other to form towering obstacles, while minibosses force you to alter your positioning on the fly. Meta-progression elements, unlocked via challenges and hidden containers, ensure that failure always feeds back into future power gains.

​Visually, the clean low-poly style allows hundreds of units to swarm the screen without performance…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks content updates and note that the developer has abandoned the project after release.

citations.review_text:
It's not only been a year since the last game update, but also since the last post or comment of the developer themselves. The dev is actually the same one as for Muck and Crab Game, but shadily created an alternate persona for this release, for some reason.

Megabonk has no actual content. The currency you earn is actually incredibly useless, and it accrues infinitely without being able to actually spend it on anything, since the in-game shop has nothing to purchase in the first place.

Don't support scummy developers like this one. Check the discussions for more info if you don't believe me. Save yourself the $10 and use it for something actually worthwhile, such as a lunch.

Overall it was a very addicting game and I did like the system of being able to toggle off any unlocks you wanted so you could target a specific build. That being said, this game got less than 6 months of support despite great sales figures. Since part of the inspiration seems to be Risk of Rain 2 and Vampire Survivors I was really thinking the entire time "oh man I can't wait to have my partner or my friends play a few rounds with me" because co-op would be a perfect fit for this game. While I can kinda understand wanting to take the money and running because you don't wanna have to work hard anymore, it does look kinda bad when your game gets published and is super insanely popular and gets abandoned in less than a year. I typically see abandonment from games that tank financially, or have terrible reviews, but Megabonk didn't suffer from either so it was really shocking to me that coming back in October 2026 there's just no further development on it. I understand not every game can be Terraria and get high quality updates for a million years but I'm disappointed that I saw so much potential in this game and it just never took off. It's still replayable and I may one day get an urge to do a few rounds again but it's just kinda sad that it could've been more. There are games that cost less (or are free) that get more attention from their devs and it is what it is, I probably won't buy from Dani again but at least I had fun for a little bit.

citation.review_text: Fun game but the final bosses for the zones are absolutely cancerous and unless you metagame it/guide it, its hard to beat them. They are designed to be anti-fun and anti-build, and force you to just metagame it, and there is no fun in that. I have alot of fun using a variety of different builds and strats up until the Tier 3 final boss, then everything is thrown out the window, and it turns into a health regen fight or kill quickly game and that is no fun. They take away your weapons except the base one (so you remember those other weapons you had fun upgrading during the 30+mins of play? Yeah useless now until the next phase allows you to use them), he throws a bunch of hard to dodge attacks at you, shrines you have to sit still and charge (while dodging attacks, and 3 spawned area bosses.. so yeah good luck with that, thats difficult unless you meta gamed fast charging shrines), and oh dont worry while your try to charge the shrines while trying to dodge large aoe attacks, the final boss is healing himself. Quickly. They took a great game, fun and varied weapons, cool characters, and ruined it with the final area bosses. Absolutely awful boss design. Do not recommend game.

citations.review_text: This is a pretty fun game that iterated on a budding genre. Danide- I mean Vedinad did an excellent job of combining elements of various rouge-likes into a fun game that I have poured numerous hours into. That being said, I would recommend getting it on sale instead of full price as it hasn't gotten an update since Feb. and likely won't given the radio silence on the devs part. If this game gets an update, that sentiment changes immediately but yeah. Its a lil rough around the edges balancing-wise and there is a lot of room for additional content that sadly was hasnt been made. Despite that, I think this game deserves to be a classic and a case study on how to make a simple yet fun game.
Incredible game! It is very hard and there are no updates, unfortunately, but I'm ready to try the mods after I get everything unlocked!
dev abandoned the game almost immediately after release

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks content and express a desire for more maps, characters, items, and tomes.

citations.review_text:
Megabonk is my favorite wave/item based action rougelike. Megabonk takes after many games that preceded it,  but in great taste. It combines many aspects from of my favorite games (Vampire Survivors-like upgrades, b-hopping, varying item builds, etc), without feeling like it is ripping them off. 

The only thing that I wish that Megabonk offered more of is content, but this is a nit-pick. Megabonk, being a $10 game, is a GREAT value. It has more than enough content for that price. I just love it so much, I often times wish there was another map, a few more characters, items, and tomes. If that is the worst thing that I have to say about the game, I think that's pretty great. 

If you like Vampire Survivors, Risk of Rain 2, or any similar game, you you most likely enjoy Megabonk. Give it a shot.
It would be hard to say anything but great things after putting 520 hours into this game.  I would love to see more content, however.

Having fun with this one. Can't put it down right now. Fun to explore different characters and item combinations. Should have been called Bunny Hopper 2000.

Cons:
- Was the strafing/bunny hopping thing the original intent or a happy accident?
- Needs way more maps
- Needs more content in general. More, damn you

citations.review_text: Fun game but you can never really compete for the front page leaderboard unless you minmax all the enjoyment out of it. Still worth a play but will be frustrating for people that are shooting for those spots
Only a few meta builds that actually apply to doing well and enjoying the game. completely left up to RNG. not a fun experience

I do recommend this game, especially if you're a casual player. It's fun and innovative, with interesting build variety.....

But, and I gotta add the but here, this ends completely when you want to try to do anything leaderboard related. The meta is so cancerously prevalent that it guts everything that makes the game fun and interesting, turning attempting an infinite run into a monotonous, boring, farm experience. 

Pros:
Fun casual gameplay, interesting strategies, build variation, hats, skins to flex on your chud friends with

Cons:
Inescapable meta at high level
